data: Surfaces are all around us, walls and ceilings of our rooms are planes, bottles are cylinders, the football in the playground is a sphere and the rugby ball is an ellipsoid, the vada we eat is a torus and the ice cream cone is, well, a cone. The shape of these objects will be studied using calculus. The course will begin with the study of curves in plane and in three-dimensional space. The concepts of length, orientation, speed, curvature, and torsion will be introduced and studied. Motivated by the study of curves, several notions of curvatures of a surface, like principal curvatures and Gaussian curvature, will be examined. Intuitively, the way a surface is curved seems to be a property of how it is embedded in space. But Gaussian curvature turns out to be intrinsic, that is, an ant confined to moving on the surface will be able to measure this quantity. This hints at the possibility of the study of shapes of higher dimensional analogues of surfaces.
